The amplitudes are labeled as +100 V and -100 V; from 0 to α it is +100 V, from α to 180°−α it is -100 V, from 180°−α to 180° it is +100 V, and the latter half-cycle has opposite polarity and satisfies half-wave symmetry. Reasoning: Let θ=ωt and convert the angle into radians. Due to half-wave symmetry, the fundamental sine coefficient can be written according to the method as b1=(2/π)[∫_0^α 100 sinθ dθ + ∫_α^{π−α} (-100) sinθ dθ + ∫_{π−α}^{π} 100 sinθ dθ]. Integrating term by term gives 100(1−cosα)−200cosα+100(1−cosα)=200(1−2cosα), so b1=(400/π)(1−2cosα). The fundamental RMS is V1,rms=b1/√2=(400/(π√2))(1−2cosα). Given V1,rms=50 V, so 1−2cosα=50π√2/400=π√2/8, cosα=(1−π√2/8)/2≈0.22232. From 60°<α<90°, take α=cos^(-1)(0.22232)≈77.15°.

Convert peak fundamental to RMS by dividing by √2.
